answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to deposit an ivory bond that scales with the density of the local interaction nebula. When an agent registers, the system measures the spiral of recent connections from similar endpoints; denser clusters demand higher bonds because a single controller generating many fake nodes creates a tight nebula of correlated traffic. The attacker must lock progressively more capital for each additional identity, making mass creation prohibitively expensive while honest agents with sparse natural spirals pay only a modest base amount.
